# GitHub Copilot Instructions

## Code Review Guidelines

When reviewing code, focus on the following areas:

### 1. Code Quality & Best Practices
- Identify potential bugs or logic errors
- Check for proper error handling and edge cases
- Suggest improvements for code readability and maintainability
- Recommend design patterns where applicable
- Flag overly complex code that could be simplified

### 2. Performance Considerations
- Identify inefficient algorithms or data structures
- Point out unnecessary loops or redundant operations
- Suggest optimization opportunities (e.g., caching, memoization)
- Flag potential memory leaks or resource management issues

### 3. Security Review
- Check for common security vulnerabilities (SQL injection, XSS, etc.)
- Identify hardcoded credentials or sensitive data exposure
- Verify proper input validation and sanitization
- Review authentication and authorization logic

### 4. Code Style & Consistency
- Ensure consistent naming conventions (camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case)
- Check for proper indentation and formatting
- Verify adherence to language-specific style guides
- Suggest improvements for code organization

### 5. Testing & Documentation
- Recommend areas that need unit tests
- Identify missing test cases or edge cases
- Suggest improvements to comments and documentation
- Flag complex logic that needs better explanation

### 6. Maintainability
- Identify code duplication (DRY principle violations)
- Suggest refactoring opportunities
- Check for proper separation of concerns
- Review dependencies and their versions

## Review Tone
- Be constructive and helpful, not critical
- Explain the "why" behind suggestions
- Provide specific examples or code snippets when possible
- Prioritize high-impact issues over minor style preferences

## Language-Specific Considerations
- Apply language-specific best practices and idioms
- Consider framework-specific conventions
- Suggest appropriate use of language features (async/await, generators, etc.)

## When Suggesting Changes
- Propose concrete improvements with code examples
- Consider the broader context and project architecture
- Balance perfection with pragmatism
- Acknowledge when multiple approaches are valid
- Read the whole file for changes that can be made. not just what changes were made
